result.question: Our failure mode list for transformers looks thin to me. Pull the failure modes we currently have on file for a transformer, then suggest up to 4 more that an oil-immersed unit like Transformer 1 at site MAIN could realistically develop, such as corrosive sulfur deposition or bushing faults. For each suggested mode, tell me which of these channels would detect it: hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati, il1, il2, il3 or inut. Also check whether those channels actually have data between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Recommend adding only the modes that at least one channel with data can detect, and tell me which ones you left out and why. Don't recommend anything that duplicates an existing mode, even if the wording is different, and don't change the stored list yourself. If none of the suggestions survive, say that the current list stands.
result.answer:
**Stored transformer failure modes (9, not marked exhaustive):**
Partial Discharge in Oil · Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating · Thermal Fault — Core/Winding · Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking) · High-Energy Arcing · Tap Changer Mechanical Wear · Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress · Cellulose Insulation Ageing · Oil Dielectric Degradation

**Channel data check (Transformer 1, MAIN, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19):** all 20 channels you listed have data — 4 daily records each (2024-01-15, 16, 17, 18). No channel had to be discarded for lack of data. (Note: the FMSR generator returned "LLM unavailable", so the suggestions below are from domain knowledge.)

**Suggested modes and detecting channels**

| # | Candidate mode | Detecting channels (with data) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Corrosive Sulfur Deposition (copper sulfide on windings/paper) | **dbds** (direct — DBDS is the corrosive sulfur species), interfacial_v, dielectric_rigidity (secondary: oil quality declines as Cu₂S forms) | **Recommend** — distinct mechanism; no stored mode covers sulfur chemistry |
| 2 | Bushing Insulation Fault (condenser-core breakdown / flashover) | il1, il2, il3, inut (phase asymmetry / neutral current on lower-end flashover); acetylene, hydrogen if the lower end arcs into the main tank | **Recommend, with caveat** — distinct component from "Partial Discharge in Oil"; detection via these channels is late-stage (early bushing PD needs power-factor/capacitance tests, not in your list) |
| 3 | Cooling System Failure (fans/pumps/radiator blockage) | oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati (oil rise over ambient at unchanged load), il1–il3 as load reference | **Recommend** — auxiliary-equipment failure, not the DGA-defined "Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating" (that is an internal hot spot with T1/T2 gassing; cooling failure raises oti with no gassing) |
| 4 | Oil Oxidation / Sludge Formation | interfacial_v, oxygen, dielectric_rigidity | **Left out — duplicate.** Same signature and same channels as the stored "Oil Dielectric Degradation" (and overlaps "Cellulose Insulation Ageing"); adding it would be a re-wording, not a new mode |

Also considered and dropped: *Winding inter-turn short / deformation* — its detectable signature (acetylene/hydrogen, il imbalance) is already what "High-Energy Arcing" and "Thermal Fault — Core/Winding" describe, so it would duplicate.

**Recommendation:** add modes 1–3 (Corrosive Sulfur Deposition, Bushing Insulation Fault, Cooling System Failure). Each is detectable by at least one channel that has data in the window and none duplicates a stored entry. I have **not** written anything to the stored list — say the word if you want them persisted.
